changes_made.explanation: Changed answer from Yes to No because this paper does NOT address NLG tasks. It focuses on tabular classification using LLMs, which is a text classification task, not natural language generation. The LLM is used to make classification predictions, not to generate natural language text.
Normalized metric names to standard forms and removed abbreviations since they refer to the same metrics. The paper uses these automatic metrics to evaluate classification performance and fairness.
No LLMs are used as judges/evaluators in this paper. GPT-3.5 is used as the classification model being evaluated, not as an evaluator of generated outputs.
The paper does not conduct any human evaluations. All evaluations are automated using fairness metrics.

overall_notes: This paper is fundamentally about fairness evaluation of LLMs for tabular classification tasks, not natural language generation. The core contribution is analyzing social biases in LLM-based classification systems. The extracted metadata was mostly accurate for Questions 2-4, but Question 1 was incorrect as this is not an NLG paper.
